marginplyr creates the grouping sets requested by a Grouping specification; it
does not create unobserved values within those sets. Complete absent keys
before a Margin operation when synthetic facts should participate in detail,
subtotal, and grand-total summaries. Replace values after a summary when the
change is only for display.

If grouping sets are new to you, read [Get
started](https://sayuks.github.io/marginplyr/vignettes/get_started.html)
first. It introduces the Grouping specifications, Margin labels, and Margin
operations this guide assumes.

```{r setup}
#| message: false

library(marginplyr)
library(dplyr)
```

Nothing beyond marginplyr's own dependencies is required. The tidyr and SQLite
sections below need optional packages, so their chunks evaluate only when those
packages are installed at the versions marginplyr asks for. Where a package is
missing or too old the code is still shown, but its output is absent.

```{r}
#| include: false

# `marginplyr_suggest_available()` answers what a bare installation check
# could not: whether the installed package satisfies the version DESCRIPTION
# requires. AGENTS.md is authoritative for which guards must go through it.
source(system.file("suggests", "guard.R", package = "marginplyr"))

has_tidyr <- marginplyr_suggest_available("tidyr")
has_sqlite <- marginplyr_suggest_available("DBI") &&
  marginplyr_suggest_available("RSQLite")
```

## Complete local facts with `tidyr::complete()`

This small fact table does not contain every product for every observed
region-store relationship:

```{r}
facts <- tibble(
  fact_id = 1:3,
  region = c("East", "East", "West"),
  store = c("A", "B", "C"),
  product = c("Laptop", "Monitor", "Laptop"),
  units = c(2L, 3L, 4L),
  revenue = c(200, 300, 400)
)

product_domain <- c("Laptop", "Monitor")
facts
```

`tidyr::nesting(region, store)` preserves only observed region-store
relationships while crossing each relationship with the product domain:

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_tidyr

completed_facts <- facts |>
  mutate(is_fact = TRUE) |>
  tidyr::complete(
    tidyr::nesting(region, store),
    product = product_domain,
    fill = list(
      is_fact = FALSE,
      units = 0L,
      revenue = 0
    )
  )

completed_facts
```

The inserted zeros now participate in every level of the rollup:

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_tidyr

completed_facts |>
  summarize_with_margins(
    rows = dplyr::n(),
    observed_facts = sum(is_fact),
    units = sum(units),
    mean_per_key = mean(revenue),
    mean_per_fact = mean(revenue[is_fact]),
    .grouping = rollup(region, store, product),
    .id = "occurrence"
  ) |>
  arrange(occurrence, region, store, product) |>
  select(region, store, product, rows, observed_facts, starts_with("mean"))
```

`rows` counts completed keys, while `observed_facts` counts only source facts.
The retained `fact_id` and `is_fact` marker make that distinction explicit.
The two means show that filling synthetic facts before a summary is a
substantive modeling choice: `mean_per_key` averages the inserted zeros in,
and `mean_per_fact` leaves them out.

If the intended change is only presentational — a row for every key, but no
synthetic fact in any summary — the rows still come from the completed input,
because a summary has no row for a key it never saw. What keeps the synthetic
facts out is the summary expression: `mean(revenue[is_fact])` averages only
the observed facts, so a completed key with none averages an empty selection
and reports `NaN`. Replace that afterwards, as `coalesce()` replaces any
missing value:

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_tidyr

observed_summary <- completed_facts |>
  summarize_with_margins(
    mean_revenue = mean(revenue[is_fact]),
    .grouping = rollup(region, store, product)
  )

observed_summary |>
  mutate(display_mean = dplyr::coalesce(mean_revenue, 0))
```

Three detail rows change; every subtotal and the grand total keep the value
they were summarized to, because that `mutate()` adds no fact rows and alters
no existing aggregate.

Completing the finished Margin result instead does not work.
`tidyr::complete()` takes each Margin label for one more value of its column,
so it crosses the labels with real values and invents rows that no grouping
set produced, each filled with a made-up zero:

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_tidyr

margin_result <- facts |>
  summarize_with_margins(
    mean_revenue = mean(revenue),
    .grouping = rollup(region, store, product)
  )

completed_result <- margin_result |>
  tidyr::complete(
    tidyr::nesting(region, store),
    product = product_domain,
    fill = list(mean_revenue = 0)
  )

c(summary_rows = nrow(margin_result), completed_rows = nrow(completed_result))

completed_result |>
  filter(store == "Total", product != "Total")
```

There is no store called `Total`, and East has no Laptop subtotal across its
stores: the rollup never asked for one. Complete the input, not the result.

## Why completion is a separate operation

marginplyr has no `.complete`, `.fill`, or `.empty` argument and no
`complete_with_margins()`. Completing the input and replacing displayed values
answer different questions — the first adds facts that every grouping set
summarizes, the second changes how a finished summary is shown — and only the
caller knows which one is meant. Nor can the first be done afterwards from the
summary: sums can be rebuilt from child sums, but a mean needs weights,
distinct counts overlap, and medians do not combine.

A Grouping specification declares which grouping sets exist, not the value
domain of each dimension. `share_of_parent()` and `share_of_total()` hold the
same line: *Value rules* in the [`share_of_parent()`
reference](https://sayuks.github.io/marginplyr/man/share_of_parent.html) states
that neither ever completes keys, so a denominator with no row behind it gives
`NA_real_` rather than a number.

## Union an explicit scaffold with observed keys

Sometimes the requested domain is an explicit relation rather than a regular
cross product. Union it with observed keys before joining so facts outside the
scaffold are not accidentally discarded:

```{r}
requested_keys <- tribble(
  ~region, ~store, ~product,
  "East", "A", "Laptop",
  "East", "A", "Monitor",
  "West", "C", "Laptop",
  "West", "C", "Monitor"
)

all_keys <- requested_keys |>
  union(distinct(facts, region, store, product))

scaffolded_facts <- all_keys |>
  left_join(facts, by = c("region", "store", "product")) |>
  mutate(
    is_fact = !is.na(fact_id),
    units = dplyr::coalesce(units, 0L),
    revenue = dplyr::coalesce(revenue, 0)
  )

scaffolded_facts
```

The `left_join()` makes one synthetic fact for every scaffold key without an
observed fact. Keep a fact identifier or marker whenever counts, means, or
other summaries must distinguish those rows.

## Complete keys on a database connection

Use ordinary lazy relations on the same connection. The domain comes from a
dimension table and a union rather than from `tidyr::complete()`: dbplyr's
`complete()` accepts only expressions over the table's own columns, so the
literal `product = product_domain` used above fails with *Every expression
must use at least one data column*. An existing dimension table is the
natural source of a reusable key domain:

```{r}
#| message: false
#| eval: !expr has_sqlite

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")

facts_db <- copy_to(
  con,
  facts,
  name = "facts",
  temporary = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)
dimension_db <- copy_to(
  con,
  requested_keys,
  name = "store_product_dimension",
  temporary = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

observed_keys_db <- facts_db |>
  distinct(region, store, product)
all_keys_db <- dimension_db |>
  select(region, store, product) |>
  union(observed_keys_db)

completed_db <- all_keys_db |>
  left_join(
    facts_db,
    by = c("region", "store", "product")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_fact = !is.na(fact_id),
    units = dplyr::coalesce(units, 0L),
    revenue = dplyr::coalesce(revenue, 0)
  )

completed_db |>
  summarize_with_margins(
    observed_facts = sum(is_fact, na.rm = TRUE),
    revenue = sum(revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    .grouping = rollup(region, store, product),
    .sort = "last"
  ) |>
  collect()

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

The union, join, completion expressions, and Margin summary stay lazy until
`collect()` runs them as one query. The result is the rollup of the facts
completed against the scaffold in the previous section, computed by the
database: two synthetic Monitor rows with no observed fact, and subtotals
that count them.

## Move local keys only when you ask to

For a small local key table, `dbplyr::copy_inline()` embeds the rows in the
lazy SQL as a `VALUES` subquery. It creates no table, so it needs no
permission to write one, but the query text grows with the number of keys:

```{r}
#| message: false
#| eval: !expr has_sqlite

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
facts_db <- copy_to(
  con,
  facts,
  name = "facts",
  temporary = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

inline_keys <- dbplyr::copy_inline(con, requested_keys)
inline_query <- inline_keys |>
  union(distinct(facts_db, region, store, product)) |>
  left_join(
    facts_db,
    by = c("region", "store", "product")
  )
show_query(inline_query)

reusable_keys <- copy_to(
  con,
  requested_keys,
  name = "requested_keys",
  temporary = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)
reusable_query <- reusable_keys |>
  union(distinct(facts_db, region, store, product)) |>
  left_join(
    facts_db,
    by = c("region", "store", "product")
  )
show_query(reusable_query)

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

Read the two renderings side by side. The inline query carries the key rows
themselves — on SQLite, a zero-row `SELECT` joined by `UNION ALL` to a
`VALUES` list, wrapped in the casts that give the columns their types — while
the `copy_to()` query names `requested_keys`, a temporary table that now
exists on the connection until it closes.

Use explicit `dplyr::copy_to()` for a larger or reusable local key relation.
It performs data movement at the line where the caller requested it.

marginplyr never copies, collects, uploads, downloads, or otherwise moves
completion data implicitly. Connection choice, data movement, and execution
remain ordinary dplyr and dbplyr operations owned by the caller.

Execution, not completion, is where each backend starts to impose rules of its
own. [Database
backends](https://sayuks.github.io/marginplyr/vignettes/database_backends.html)
takes the lazy pipeline from here through query shape, `collect()`, and what
each backend is verified to do.
